name: Retainer wear nightly

card.summary: Wearing a retainer at night after braces or aligners to hold teeth in place; orthodontic sources describe relapse risk as lifelong.
card.note: Wear schedules are set by the treating orthodontist.

quick.overview:
After teeth are moved, they tend to drift back toward their old positions. Retainers are worn to hold the corrected alignment, and many orthodontists advise nightly wear for years after full-time wear.

In looksmaxxing circles it is framed as the way to keep results from relapse after braces or aligners.
quick.mechanism: Retainers resist relapse forces from recoil of the periodontal fibres, soft-tissue pressure, the bite and continued growth. Removable types are worn at set times; fixed types are bonded behind the front teeth.
quick.risks: Poor cleaning can cause plaque, cavities and gum inflammation. Clear retainers worn while eating can trap sugary or acidic substances, and hot water can distort them. Grinding can break them quickly.

lead: Wearing a retainer at night holds teeth in the positions that braces or aligners achieved, so a straight, aligned smile stays that way. For anyone who has paid for orthodontic work, nightly retainer use is the routine that protects the result. Orthodontic sources describe a lifelong tendency for teeth to drift back, caused by elastic recoil of periodontal fibres, pressure from soft tissue, the bite and continued growth [1]. One overview states that more than half of patients show some reversion within ten years [2].

Removable retainers include Hawley types (a wire on an acrylic palate) and vacuum-formed clear shells; fixed retainers are wires bonded behind the front teeth. Vacuum-formed retainers are usually worn overnight and removed for meals, and the schedule can be fixed-term or indefinite as set by the orthodontist [1]. One overview suggests about six months of full-time wear followed by nighttime wear for many years [2].

Systematic reviews have compared retainer types and found fixed retainers perform best, with vacuum-formed retainers holding lower incisors better than other removable types [1]. Nightly-only schedules specifically have not been the subject of a dedicated trial in the material reviewed.

angle.text: People wear retainers overnight to keep corrected tooth alignment. The visible payoff is an even, straight smile years after braces or aligners come off.

infobox: Hawley, vacuum-formed, Begg, Barrer, fixed bonded wire [1]
Vacuum-formed types are cheaper than other removable types [1]

paras: Hawley retainers, named for Charles A. Hawley and among the oldest designs, are durable and adjustable but less attractive, can affect speech and are prone to fracture; a clear-wire version exists. Vacuum-formed retainers are nearly invisible clear shells that cover the biting surfaces, cost less and interfere less with speech, though they can crack in people who grind their teeth. Begg and Barrer retainers are other removable designs, and SMART retainers pair a sensor case with a phone app that tracks wear. Fixed retainers are wires bonded behind the front teeth, used where relapse risk is higher, such as severe rotations or gaps; they do not rely on patient cooperation but are harder to clean [1].

Removable retainers can be worn full-time or part-time as the orthodontist advises, and the period may be set or indefinite [1]. Because relapse is described as lifelong, many orthodontists prescribe night wear long term [1][2]. A T Nation forum member mentions wearing Invisalign retainers at night and removing them in the morning [3].

A 2020 systematic review of randomized trials found Hawley retainers did not effectively prevent relapse of incisor crowding. A 2018 systematic review found vacuum-formed retainers held lower incisors better than other removable types, with fixed retainers performing best. A 2016 Cochrane review reported patients found Hawley retainers more embarrassing and harder to wear than vacuum-formed ones, and a 2018 review found Hawley retainers can affect certain sounds, a smaller issue when worn only at night [1]. Compliance is the main practical concern [1].

Poor cleaning can cause plaque, cavities and gum inflammation. Vacuum-formed retainers worn while eating or inserted right after a meal or sugary drink can trap cariogenic substances; grinding can break them and hot water can shrink them. Orthodontic sources advise brushing removable retainers gently with non-abrasive toothpaste or mild soap and storing them dry [1].
Systematic reviews, including a 2016 Cochrane review of retention procedures and 2018 and 2020 reviews, have compared retainer types [1]. No studies found specifically on nightly-only wear schedules.
